subject: literature
passage: For forty years, Anselm had opened his clock shop at seven each morning. When his daughter suggested over dinner that he finally close it and rest, he said nothing at all. The next morning she found him at his bench as usual, bent over the gears of a neighbor's mantel clock. He did not argue with her or explain himself; he simply kept working, as if the matter had been settled. His refusal was ______ but unmistakable.
stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?

explanation.why: Anselm "said nothing," "did not argue with her or explain himself," and simply went back to work. The sentence contrasts the manner of his refusal with how clear it was ("but unmistakable"), so the blank must describe a refusal given without words: "unspoken."
explanation.A: Incorrect. Anselm "did not argue" with his daughter, and nothing suggests anger or unfriendliness toward her.
explanation.B: Incorrect. Anselm returned to work the very next morning "as if the matter had been settled," so his refusal shows no hesitation.
explanation.C: Incorrect. An elaborate refusal would involve many words or explanations, but Anselm "said nothing at all."
explanation.D: Correct. Anselm never put his refusal into words; he showed it by returning to his bench. An unspoken refusal can still be unmistakable.
